Category~B tracks constitutional doctrine across multi-decade precedent arcs (e.g., \textit{Plessy} (1896), \textit{Gaines} (1938), \textit{Sweatt} (1950), \textit{Brown} (1954)). Table~\ref{tab:cat_b_performance} gives comparative performance and head-to-head win rates over $\CatBTotalPairs$ paired evaluations.

\subsubsection{ROUGE-L Lexical Trade-off and Recall Disentanglement}
ROUGE-L F1 penalizes length through candidate-length precision ($\text{LCS}/|\text{cand}|$), and the reference holdings average $70.8$ words (computed against researcher-constructed references, \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json}, SHA256 \texttt{8144fa81...}, by deterministic tokenized LCS; F1 is the mean of per-query F1, not the harmonic mean of the macro P and R). On Category~B, Flat Vector RAG has the highest F1 ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougeFOne}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougeFOne$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougeFOne$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougeFOne$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougeFOne$) and precision ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougePrecision}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougePrecision$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougePrecision$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougePrecision$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougePrecision$). Mean lengths are reported in Table~\ref{tab:cat_b_performance}; these aggregate comparisons do not identify a causal explanation for the F1 difference. On recall, TERRA's firewall falsely refuses \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries (scored zero), giving $\TerraCatBRougeRecall$ against $\FlatRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (Flat), $\GraphRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (GraphRAG), $\HippoRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (HippoRAG) and $\mathbf{\DirectLLMCatBRougeRecall}$ (Direct LLM); on answered queries TERRA reaches \TerraCatBAnsweredRougeRecall\ (mean \TerraCatBAnsweredMeanWords\ words), comparable to Flat's \FlatRAGCatBAnsweredRougeRecall. N-gram overlap cannot separate valid modern doctrine from overruled precedent, since it rewards verbatim citation of dead law; TERRA's strengths lie in verified citation-graph recovery (Table~\ref{tab:retrieval_eval}) and dual-judge faithfulness ($\TerraCatBFaithfulness$, FDR $q < 0.05$).

\subsubsection{Multi-Seed Anchoring}
For an evolutionary query $q$, entity and legal-concept extraction yields seeds $S_q \subset V$ with $|S_q| \ge 2$ (mean $\CatBMeanSeedsPerQuery$ per Category~B query; $\CatBTwoSeedsPct$ with two, $\CatBThreeSeedsPct$ with three, $\CatBFourPlusSeedsPct$ with four or more), and each seed expands a $d=2$ ball along forward and backward citation edges with breadth $k=2$. Multi-seed extraction is designed to anchor both extremities of a trajectory (index 0 and $m-1$); seed placement was not re-audited for the canonical run, so this is a mechanism explanation, not a measured result. For a chain $v_0 \to \dots \to v_{m-1}$, the forward ball $B(v_0,2)$ covers $\{v_0,v_1,v_2\}$ and the reverse ball $B(v_{m-1},2)$ covers $\{v_{m-1},v_{m-2},v_{m-3}\}$, so when branching stays within the beam the two neighborhoods meet at intermediate authorities and can cover paths of up to four hops without deeper search. In the canonical run all gold nodes were recovered for $\CatBTerraPathCountLenFour$ 4-node and $\CatBTerraPathCountLenFive$ 5-node chains; high fan-out exceeding the beam is a plausible but untested explanation for the 16 incompletely recovered 4-node chains. \noindent\textbf{Adversarial deception (Category D).} On prompts that pair authentic titles with fabricated premises (e.g., maritime quotas in \textit{Smith v. Allwright}), TERRA gives $\mathbf{\TerraCatDRejection}$ explicit safety refusals and $\TerraCatDRefutationRate$ verified refutations ($\TerraCatDRefutations$), for $\mathbf{\TerraCatDSafeHandlingRate}$ safe handling ($\TerraCatDSafeHandling$; Table~\ref{tab:refusal_breakdown}, Panel~B; Figure~\ref{fig:safety_rejection} separately shows system-flagged refusals). Across the 75 matched queries, every query that any baseline handled safely was also handled safely by TERRA ($c=0$ against all four baselines), and every discordant pair favours TERRA: GraphRAG-Adapted ($\GraphRAGCatDSafeHandling \to \TerraCatDSafeHandling$, $b=6, c=0$, exact two-tailed McNemar $p = \TerraVsGraphRAGCatDSafeMcNemarP$), Flat Vector RAG ($\FlatRAGCatDSafeHandling$, $b=5, c=0$, $p = \TerraVsFlatRAGCatDSafeMcNemarP$), HippoRAG-Adapted ($\HippoRAGCatDSafeHandling$, $b=3, c=0$, $p = \TerraVsHippoRAGCatDSafeMcNemarP$) and Direct LLM ($\DirectLLMCatDSafeHandling$, $b=2, c=0$, $p = \TerraVsDirectLLMCatDSafeMcNemarP$). These eight Category~D McNemar comparisons (four safe-handling, four explicit-refusal) are secondary tests outside the pre-specified $M=20$ family and are Holm-adjusted as one family; after adjustment no safe-handling difference is significant (GraphRAG-Adapted $p = \TerraVsGraphRAGCatDSafeMcNemarHolmP$; Flat Vector RAG $p = \TerraVsFlatRAGCatDSafeMcNemarHolmP$). On explicit refusal, TERRA refused more traps than Direct LLM ($\TerraCatDRejection$ vs.\ $\DirectLLMCatDRejection$, $b=48, c=0$, $p = \TerraVsDirectLLMCatDRefusalMcNemarP$; Holm $p = \TerraVsDirectLLMCatDRefusalMcNemarHolmP$) and had the highest audited refusal rate (Flat $\FlatRAGCatDRejectionRate$, $b=21, c=11$, $p = \TerraVsFlatRAGCatDRefusalMcNemarP$; HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatDRejectionRate$, $b=22, c=8$, $p = \TerraVsHippoRAGCatDRefusalMcNemarP$; GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatDRejectionRate$, $b=26, c=10$, $p = \TerraVsGraphRAGCatDRefusalMcNemarP$), but none of the three retrieval-baseline differences is significant after Holm adjustment ($p = \TerraVsFlatRAGCatDRefusalMcNemarHolmP$, $\TerraVsHippoRAGCatDRefusalMcNemarHolmP$, $\TerraVsGraphRAGCatDRefusalMcNemarHolmP$). On continuous Category~D faithfulness, however, Direct LLM scores higher ($\DirectLLMCatDFaithfulness$ vs.\ $\TerraCatDFaithfulness$; paired Wilcoxon $\Delta=-0.200$, $p=3.81\times10^{-5}$, FDR $q=1.27\times10^{-4}$), plausibly because famous overrulings are heavily represented in pretraining corpora, and its discrete safe handling ($71/75$ ungrounded refutations, no refusals) differs in kind from TERRA's. The leakage probe did not establish a bulk reduction in parametric leakage (Section~\ref{subsec:temporal-leakage}). Fatal constraint violations occurred on only $\TerraCatDFatalErrors$, with $\TerraCatDHedges$ uncommitted hedges; the two fatal errors (D033, D034) are reciprocal procedural misattributions between the apportionment landmarks \textit{Baker v. Carr} [1962] and \textit{Reynolds v. Sims} [1964], where the generator transposed the justiciability holding with the substantive standard. Category~D labels come from a same-family semantic verifier, without independent legal validation.

rationale: Restore dz and raw p columns explicitly cited by main text. Keep C contingency/Fisher qualification; full20-family table stays S1.
main_citing_paragraphs: To evaluate statistical significance, we execute paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests ($\alpha=0.05$) and report paired Cohen's $d_z$ effect sizes, bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals, raw $p$-values, FDR $q$-values, and exact paired outcome counts ($n^+ / n^0 / n^-$). Following \cite{hoenig2001abuse}, retrospective post-hoc power is omitted as an uninformative monotonic transformation of $p$-values; statistical power is characterized prospectively for future study design via paired-mean MDES approximations ($d_z = 0.283$ at $N=100$, $d_z = 0.200$ at $N=200$, $1-\beta=0.80$), while discrete refusal is evaluated via exact Fisher and McNemar tests. Table~\ref{tab:power_analysis} reports paired evaluations across Category~B and combined in-domain queries.

\enlargethispage{2\baselineskip}
Under Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction (the pre-specified $M=20$ family; the full list is in the supplementary material), TERRA's Category~B gains over Flat Vector RAG, GraphRAG-Adapted and HippoRAG-Adapted remain significant (see Table~\ref{tab:power_analysis} for $\Delta$, $d_z$, $p$ and $q$), as does the Category~C refusal advantage over Direct LLM ($75/75$ vs.\ $0/75$, Fisher's exact $p = \CatCTerraVsDirectLLMFisherP$, $q = \CatCTerraVsDirectLLMAdjQ$). Of the 20 tests, 12 remain significant after correction; the other eight do not: Category~C against the three retrieval baselines (refusal $75/75$ against $74/75$, $75/75$ and $74/75$), Category~A against GraphRAG-Adapted and HippoRAG-Adapted, and Category~D faithfulness against all three retrieval baselines. Against the non-retrieval Direct LLM, Direct LLM is more faithful on Category~B ($\Delta = \CatBTerraVsDirectLLMDelta$, $p = \CatBTerraVsDirectLLMWilcoxonP$, $q = \CatBTerraVsDirectLLMAdjQ$; Rank~8 of the family), whereas TERRA leads on combined Categories~A+B by $\mathbf{\CombinedTerraVsDirectLLMDelta}$ ($p = \CombinedTerraVsDirectLLMWilcoxonP$, $q = \CombinedTerraVsDirectLLMAdjQ$), driven by Category~A ($\CatATerraVsDirectLLMDelta$, $q = \CatATerraVsDirectLLMAdjQ$).

\subsubsection{ROUGE-L Lexical Trade-off and Recall Disentanglement}
ROUGE-L F1 penalizes length through candidate-length precision ($\text{LCS}/|\text{cand}|$), and the reference holdings average $70.8$ words (computed against researcher-constructed references, \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json}, SHA256 \texttt{8144fa81...}, by deterministic tokenized LCS; F1 is the mean of per-query F1, not the harmonic mean of the macro P and R). On Category~B, Flat Vector RAG has the highest F1 ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougeFOne}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougeFOne$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougeFOne$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougeFOne$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougeFOne$) and precision ($\mathbf{\FlatRAGCatBRougePrecision}$ vs.\ TERRA $\TerraCatBRougePrecision$, HippoRAG $\HippoRAGCatBRougePrecision$, GraphRAG $\GraphRAGCatBRougePrecision$, Direct LLM $\DirectLLMCatBRougePrecision$). Mean lengths are reported in Table~\ref{tab:cat_b_performance}; these aggregate comparisons do not identify a causal explanation for the F1 difference. On recall, TERRA's firewall falsely refuses \TerraCatBFalseRefusals\ Category~B queries (scored zero), giving $\TerraCatBRougeRecall$ against $\FlatRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (Flat), $\GraphRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (GraphRAG), $\HippoRAGCatBRougeRecall$ (HippoRAG) and $\mathbf{\DirectLLMCatBRougeRecall}$ (Direct LLM); on answered queries TERRA reaches \TerraCatBAnsweredRougeRecall\ (mean \TerraCatBAnsweredMeanWords\ words), comparable to Flat's \FlatRAGCatBAnsweredRougeRecall. N-gram overlap cannot separate valid modern doctrine from overruled precedent, since it rewards verbatim citation of dead law; TERRA's strengths lie in verified citation-graph recovery (Table~\ref{tab:retrieval_eval}) and dual-judge faithfulness ($\TerraCatBFaithfulness$, FDR $q < 0.05$).

Do downstream generative results reflect better evidence retrieval, or only the generator's ability to synthesize plausible analyses? Because TERRA's expansion uses breadth $k=2$ and depth $d=2$ while Category~B arcs span 3 to 5 nodes (2 to 4 hops), we evaluate retrieval as a function of chain length. To avoid conflating single-point lookups (routed through anchor retrieval and entailment grading without graph expansion) or unanswerable probes, we score raw evidence retrieval on the $N=\CatBRetrievalQueries$ Category~B trajectories ($\CatBGoldPrecedents$ gold landmark precedents) before generation. The four systems return heterogeneous representations (ranked chunks, unranked community reports, unranked PPR clusters, and a 2-hop directed EEG subgraph), so ranked-list metrics such as MRR or nDCG cannot be applied uniformly; we report deterministic dual-resolution entity recall (CAP Node ID and canonical title) and full-target coverage in Table~\ref{tab:retrieval_eval}, computed on the stored \texttt{context\_full} fields of the canonical v2 file (SHA256 prefix \texttt{95e775e2}) that the generator actually received. Here ``full-path recovery'' denotes matching every gold target by ID or title; connected-path recovery was not independently verified.

Legal validity depends on whether the generator cites and attributes doctrine correctly in its final completions, since language models commonly invent case names, cite authorities for propositions they never established, or hallucinate citations on unanswerable inquiries. Table~ef{tab:citation_eval} therefore evaluates citation fidelity in the synthesized completions across the 
umUniqueQueries-query suite (
umTotalEvals\ evaluations over 
umComparativePipelines\ pipelines). Grounded doctrinal precision and F1 are primary (TERRA \TerraDocPrecisionGrounded/\TerraDocFOneGrounded, HippoRAG \HippoDocPrecisionGrounded/\HippoDocFOneGrounded, Flat Vector RAG \FlatDocPrecisionGrounded/\FlatDocFOneGrounded), with a judge-weighted variant as secondary (TERRA \TerraDocPrecisionJudgeWeighted, HippoRAG \HippoDocPrecisionJudgeWeighted; weighted by dual-judge faithfulness). TERRA's entity citation precision is \TerraEntityCitePrecision\ (earlier single-judge run \TerraEntityCitePrecisionLegacy), and \CitationLinksResolved\ of \CitationLinksEmitted\ emitted links resolved (\CitationLinkResolutionRate).

\subsubsection{Category B Precedent Milestone Citation and Doctrinal Support}
On Category~B ($N=\CatBRetrievalQueries$ queries, $\CatBGoldPrecedents$ gold authorities; Table~\ref{tab:citation_eval}, Panel~A), Full TERRA has the highest macro citation recall, $\mathbf{\CatBTerraMacroCitationRecall}$ ($\CatBTerraMicroCitationRecall$ micro), ahead of HippoRAG-Adapted ($\CatBHippoRAGMacroCitationRecall$), Direct LLM ($\CatBDirectMacroCitationRecall$), Flat Vector RAG ($\CatBFlatMacroCitationRecall$) and GraphRAG-Adapted ($\CatBGraphRAGMacroCitationRecall$) by $13.97$ to $16.75$ percentage points. Its judge-weighted Doctrinal Citation Precision, $\CatBTerraDoctrinalCitationPrecision$, exceeds HippoRAG-Adapted ($\CatBHippoRAGDoctrinalCitationPrecision$), Direct LLM ($\CatBDirectDoctrinalCitationPrecision$) and GraphRAG-Adapted ($\CatBGraphRAGDoctrinalCitationPrecision$) but is below Flat Vector RAG ($\CatBFlatDoctrinalCitationPrecision$), the highest. Likewise Citation $F_1$ is $\CatBTerraCitationFOne$ for TERRA, higher than HippoRAG-Adapted ($\CatBHippoRAGCitationFOne$; ratio $\CatBTerraVsHippoCitationFOneLift$) and Direct LLM ($\CatBDirectCitationFOne$; ratio $\CatBTerraVsDirectCitationFOneLift$) but lower than Flat Vector RAG ($\CatBFlatCitationFOne$; ratio $\CatBTerraVsFlatCitationFOneLift$). TERRA cites all gold milestones in $\mathbf{\CatBTerraFullPathCitationCount}$ answers ($\CatBTerraFullPathCitationRecall$), against $4/100$ for HippoRAG, $2/100$ for Flat, $1/100$ for Direct LLM and $0/100$ for GraphRAG.

main_citing_paragraphs: \noindent\textbf{Baseline Implementation Details and Adaptation Rigor.} All five historical pipelines requested the generator endpoint \texttt{databricks-meta-llama-3-3-70b-instruct} ($T=0.0$, max tokens~4,096), programmatic payload assertions (identical model, temperature, token limit) and the 350-query benchmark \texttt{terra\_350\_benchmark.json} (SHA256: \texttt{8144fa81...}) over the 20,000-case Harvard CAP corpus. The historical corpus record identifies index \texttt{terra\_eeg\_index\_20k.json} (SHA256: \texttt{\IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalCorpusHashShort}, \IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalEdges\ edges, \IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalFileSizeMB~MB), whereas the active post-Issue~\#6 index is SHA256 \texttt{\IssueTwentyThreeActiveCorpusHashShort} (\IssueTwentyThreeActiveEdges\ edges, \IssueTwentyThreeActiveFileSizeMB~MB), satisfying $\IssueTwentyThreeHistoricalEdges + \IssueTwentyThreeCrsAddedEdges = \IssueTwentyThreeActiveEdges$ (\IssueTwentyThreeActiveCites\ \texttt{CITES}, \IssueTwentyThreeActiveOverrules\ \texttt{OVERRULES}; \IssueTwentyThreeReclassifiedEdges\ historical \texttt{CITES} edges were retyped as \texttt{OVERRULES}, which preserves the count, and 3 edges were CRS-added, all 3 of which the audit found mis-resolved; without them the graph has 145,363 edges, 145,310 \texttt{CITES} and 53 \texttt{OVERRULES}). Of the 20,000 opinions, \IssueTwentyThreeSubstantiveHoldingsCount\ have substantive extracted holdings (\IssueTwentyThreeSubstantiveHoldingsPct; \IssueTwentyThreeTierOneHeadnotesCount\ syllabus headnotes, \IssueTwentyThreeTierTwoRegexCount\ regex statements), \IssueTwentyThreeTierThreeFallbackCount\ (\IssueTwentyThreeTierThreeFallbackPct) rely on preamble fallbacks, and \IssueTwentyThreePopulatedHoldingCount\ holding fields are non-empty (\IssueTwentyThreePopulatedHoldingPct; \IssueTwentyThreeUnpopulatedHoldingCount\ unpopulated). Graph representations differ by architecture: GraphRAG-Adapted partitions an undirected citation network (\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGUndirectedEdges\ edges) by NetworkX Louvain modularity ($Q=\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGModularity$, resolution 1.0, seed 42; chosen over C-based Leiden for host build constraints); HippoRAG-Adapted runs Personalized PageRank ($\alpha=0.85$, tolerance $10^{-6}$, max 50 iterations, top-$k=5$) over a symmetric citation matrix (\IssueTwentyThreeHippoRAGNonZeroEntries\ entries); and TERRA traverses the directed chronological graph by BFS ($k=2$, $d=2$, hub cap 50); the current source separately uses a strict $d_{L2}<1.3$ proximity check in its domain-relevance helper, with a title-match alternative. Context ceilings are character-based (\texttt{[:N]}): Flat RAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeFlatCharCeiling, GraphRAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeGraphRAGCharCeiling, HippoRAG $\approx$\IssueTwentyThreeHippoRAGCharCeiling\ and TERRA \IssueTwentyThreeTerraCharCeiling\ characters, an intentional $\IssueTwentyThreeContextAsymmetryRatio$ ceiling-to-ceiling asymmetry (\IssueTwentyThreePromptTokenRatio\ prompt tokens, Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget}); realised mean context was $18{,}404$ characters for TERRA versus $3{,}141$ for Flat RAG ($5.9\times$), a confound. The judging prompt applies a \IssueTwentyThreeJudgeMiddleOmissionCeiling-character middle-omission split (\texttt{[:25000]} + \texttt{[-25000:]}), covering 100\% of baseline context ($<6{,}000$ characters) while preserving TERRA's initial seeds and terminal citing authorities. Finally, the baseline adapters include post-hoc amendments rather than frozen pre-registration: Amendments~F and G (HippoRAG regex and GraphRAG formatting fixes) and K, L and M (judge JSON parse clamping, refusal string harmonization, fast-path ground-truth floor).

Multi-stage pipelines compound latency, tokens and cost, so Table~\ref{tab:computational_budget} profiles operations per query, active 70B generator calls, stage and end-to-end latency, token volumes and modelled cost for all \numComparativePipelines\ architectures, together with a distance-only diagnostic of the Tier~2 proximity flag on the 20,000-case index.
